ESV.1: Some time after this, the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and his baker committed an offense against their lord the king of Egypt.
ESV.2: And Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker,
ESV.3: and he put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, in the prison where Joseph was confined.
ESV.4: The captain of the guard appointed Joseph to be with them, and he attended them. They continued for some time in custody.
ESV.5: And one night they both dreamed — the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were confined in the prison — each his own dream, and each dream with its own interpretation.
ESV.6: When Joseph came to them in the morning, he saw that they were troubled.
ESV.7: So he asked Pharaoh's officers who were with him in custody in his master's house, “Why are your faces downcast today?”
ESV.8: They said to him, “We have had dreams, and there is no one to interpret them.” And Joseph said to them, “Do not interpretations belong to God? Please tell them to me.”
ESV.9: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph and said to him, “In my dream there was a vine before me,
ESV.10: and on the vine there were three branches. As soon as it budded, its blossoms shot forth, and the clusters ripened into grapes.
ESV.11: Pharaoh's cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup and placed the cup in Pharaoh's hand.”
ESV.12: Then Joseph said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
ESV.13: In three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your office, and you shall place Pharaoh's cup in his hand as formerly, when you were his cupbearer.
ESV.14: Only remember me, when it is well with you, and please do me the kindness to mention me to Pharaoh, and so get me out of this house.
ESV.15: For I was indeed stolen out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the pit.”
ESV.16: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favorable, he said to Joseph, “I also had a dream: there were three cake baskets on my head,
ESV.17: and in the uppermost basket there were all sorts of baked food for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating it out of the basket on my head.”
ESV.18: And Joseph answered and said, “This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
ESV.19: In three days Pharaoh will lift up your head — from you! — and hang you on a tree. And the birds will eat the flesh from you.”
ESV.20: On the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday, he made a feast for all his servants and lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
ESV.21: He restored the chief cupbearer to his position, and he placed the cup in Pharaoh's hand.
ESV.22: But he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
ESV.23: Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.

NKJV.1: It came to pass after these things that the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
NKJV.2: And Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief butler and the chief baker.
NKJV.3: So he put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, in the prison, the place where Joseph was confined.
NKJV.4: And the captain of the guard charged Joseph with them, and he served them; so they were in custody for a while.
NKJV.5: Then the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were confined in the prison, had a dream, both of them, each man’s dream in one night and each man’s dream with its own interpretation.
NKJV.6: And Joseph came in to them in the morning and looked at them, and saw that they were sad.
NKJV.7: So he asked Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in the custody of his lord’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”
NKJV.8: And they said to him, “We each have had a dream, and there is no interpreter of it.” So Joseph said to them, “Do not interpretations belong to God? Tell them to me, please.”
NKJV.9: Then the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “Behold, in my dream a vine was before me,
NKJV.10: and in the vine were three branches; it was as though it budded, its blossoms shot forth, and its clusters brought forth ripe grapes.
NKJV.11: Then Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.”
NKJV.12: And Joseph said to him, “This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days.
NKJV.13: Now within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your place, and you will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand according to the former manner, when you were his butler.
NKJV.14: But remember me when it is well with you, and please show kindness to me; make mention of me to Pharaoh, and get me out of this house.
NKJV.15: For indeed I was stolen away from the land of the Hebrews; and also I have done nothing here that they should put me into the dungeon.”
NKJV.16: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, “I also was in my dream, and there were three white baskets on my head.
NKJV.17: In the uppermost basket were all kinds of baked goods for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.”
NKJV.18: So Joseph answered and said, “This is the interpretation of it: The three baskets are three days.
NKJV.19: Within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head from you and hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat your flesh from you.”
NKJV.20: Now it came to pass on the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants; and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and of the chief baker among his servants.
NKJV.21: Then he restored the chief butler to his butlership again, and he placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.
NKJV.22: But he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
NKJV.23: Yet the chief butler did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.

NASB.1: Then it came about after these things, the cupbearer and the baker for the king of Egypt offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
NASB.2: Pharaoh was furious with his two officials, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
NASB.3: So he put them in confinement in the house of the captain of the bodyguard, in the jail, the [same] place where Joseph was imprisoned.
NASB.4: The captain of the bodyguard put Joseph in charge of them, and he took care of them; and they were in confinement for some time.
NASB.5: Then the cupbearer and the baker for the king of Egypt, who were confined in jail, both had a dream the same night, each man with his [own] dream [and] each dream with its [own] interpretation.
NASB.6: When Joseph came to them in the morning and observed them, behold, they were dejected.
NASB.7: He asked Pharaoh's officials who were with him in confinement in his master's house, 'Why are your faces so sad today?'
NASB.8: Then they said to him, 'We have had a dream and there is no one to interpret it.' Then Joseph said to them, 'Do not interpretations belong to God? Tell [it] to me, please.'
NASB.9: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, 'In my dream, behold, [there was] a vine in front of me;
NASB.10: and on the vine [were] three branches. And as it was budding, its blossoms came out, [and] its clusters produced ripe grapes.
NASB.11: 'Now Pharaoh's cup was in my hand; so I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I put the cup into Pharaoh's hand.'
NASB.12: Then Joseph said to him, 'This is the interpretation of it: the three branches are three days;
NASB.13: within three more days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your office; and you will put Pharaoh's cup into his hand according to your former custom when you were his cupbearer.
NASB.14: 'Only keep me in mind when it goes well with you, and please do me a kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh and get me out of this house.
NASB.15: 'For I was in fact kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing that they should have put me into the dungeon.'
NASB.16: When the chief baker saw that he had interpreted favorably, he said to Joseph, 'I also [saw] in my dream, and behold, [there were] three baskets of white bread on my head;
NASB.17: and in the top basket [there were] some of all sorts of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.'
NASB.18: Then Joseph answered and said, 'This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days;
NASB.19: within three more days Pharaoh will lift up your head from you and will hang you on a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh off you.'
NASB.20: Thus it came about on the third day, [which was] Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants; and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
NASB.21: He restored the chief cupbearer to his office, and he put the cup into Pharaoh's hand;
NASB.22: but he hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.
NASB.23: Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.

WEB.1: After these things, the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
WEB.2: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cup bearer and the chief baker.
WEB.3: He put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.
WEB.4: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he took care of them. They stayed in prison many days.
WEB.5: They both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cup bearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.
WEB.6: Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and saw that they were sad.
WEB.7: He asked Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”
WEB.8: They said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it.” Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me.”
WEB.9: The chief cup bearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was in front of me,
WEB.10: and in the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.
WEB.11: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.”
WEB.12: Joseph said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
WEB.13: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head, and restore you to your office. You will give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, the way you did when you were his cup bearer.
WEB.14: But remember me when it will be well with you, and please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
WEB.15: For indeed, I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”
WEB.16: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, “I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.
WEB.17: In the uppermost basket there were all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.”
WEB.18: Joseph answered, “This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.
WEB.19: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you, and will hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat your flesh from off you.”
WEB.20: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cup bearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
WEB.21: He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;
WEB.22: but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
WEB.23: Yet the chief cup bearer didn’t remember Joseph, but forgot him.

NLT.1: Some time later, Pharaoh’s chief cup-bearer and chief baker offended their royal master.
NLT.2: Pharaoh became angry with these two officials,
NLT.3: and he put them in the prison where Joseph was, in the palace of the captain of the guard.
NLT.4: They remained in prison for quite some time, and the captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, who looked after them.
NLT.5: While they were in prison, Pharaoh’s cup-bearer and baker each had a dream one night, and each dream had its own meaning.
NLT.6: When Joseph saw them the next morning, he noticed that they both looked upset.
NLT.7: “Why do you look so worried today?” he asked them.
NLT.8: And they replied, “We both had dreams last night, but no one can tell us what they mean.” “Interpreting dreams is God’s business,” Joseph replied. “Go ahead and tell me your dreams.”
NLT.9: So the chief cup-bearer told Joseph his dream first. “In my dream,” he said, “I saw a grapevine in front of me.
NLT.10: The vine had three branches that began to bud and blossom, and soon it produced clusters of ripe grapes.
NLT.11: I was holding Pharaoh’s wine cup in my hand, so I took a cluster of grapes and squeezed the juice into the cup. Then I placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.”
NLT.12: “This is what the dream means,” Joseph said. “The three branches represent three days.
NLT.13: Within three days Pharaoh will lift you up and restore you to your position as his chief cup-bearer.
NLT.14: And please remember me and do me a favor when things go well for you. Mention me to Pharaoh, so he might let me out of this place.
NLT.15: For I was kidnapped from my homeland, the land of the Hebrews, and now I’m here in prison, but I did nothing to deserve it.”
NLT.16: When the chief baker saw that Joseph had given the first dream such a positive interpretation, he said to Joseph, “I had a dream, too. In my dream there were three baskets of white pastries stacked on my head.
NLT.17: The top basket contained all kinds of pastries for Pharaoh, but the birds came and ate them from the basket on my head.”
NLT.18: “This is what the dream means,” Joseph told him. “The three baskets also represent three days.
NLT.19: Three days from now Pharaoh will lift you up and impale your body on a pole. Then birds will come and peck away at your flesh.”
NLT.20: Pharaoh’s birthday came three days later, and he prepared a banquet for all his officials and staff. He summoned his chief cup-bearer and chief baker to join the other officials.
NLT.21: He then restored the chief cup-bearer to his former position, so he could again hand Pharaoh his cup.
NLT.22: But Pharaoh impaled the chief baker, just as Joseph had predicted when he interpreted his dream.
NLT.23: Pharaoh’s chief cup-bearer, however, forgot all about Joseph, never giving him another thought.

CSB17.1: After this, the king of Egypt’s cupbearer <sup>ⓗ</sup> and baker offended their master, the king of Egypt.
CSB17.2: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker,
CSB17.3: and put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guards <sup>ⓘ</sup> in the prison where Joseph was confined.
CSB17.4: The captain of the guards assigned Joseph to them as their personal attendant, and they were in custody for some time. <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.5: The king of Egypt’s cupbearer and baker, who were confined in the prison, each had a dream. Both had a dream on the same night, and each dream had its own meaning.
CSB17.6: When Joseph came to them in the morning, he saw that they looked distraught.
CSB17.7: So he asked Pharaoh’s officers who were in custody with him in his master’s house, “Why do you look so sad today?” <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.8: “We had dreams,” they said to him, “but there is no one to interpret them.” Then Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.” <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.9: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph: “In my dream there was a vine in front of me.
CSB17.10: On the vine were three branches. As soon as it budded, its blossoms came out and its clusters ripened into grapes.
CSB17.11: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes, squeezed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.”
CSB17.12: “This is its interpretation,” <sup>ⓛ</sup> Joseph said to him. “The three branches are three days.
CSB17.13: In just three days Pharaoh will lift up your head <sup>ⓜ</sup> and restore you to your position. You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand the way you used to when you were his cupbearer.
CSB17.14: But when all goes well for you, remember that I was with you. Please show kindness to me by mentioning me to Pharaoh, and get me out of this prison.
CSB17.15: For I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, <sup>ⓝ</sup> and even here I have done nothing that they should put me in the dungeon.” <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.16: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was positive, he said to Joseph, “I also had a dream. Three baskets of white bread were on my head.
CSB17.17: In the top basket were all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.”
CSB17.18: “This is its interpretation,” Joseph replied. “The three baskets are three days.
CSB17.19: In just three days Pharaoh will lift up your head — from off you — and hang you on a tree. <sup>[3]</sup> Then the birds will eat the flesh from your body.” <sup>[4]</sup>
CSB17.20: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he gave a feast for all his servants. He elevated <sup>[5]</sup> the chief cupbearer and the chief baker among his servants. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.21: Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his position as cupbearer, and he placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.
CSB17.22: But Pharaoh hanged <sup>[6]</sup> the chief baker, just as Joseph had explained to them.
CSB17.23: Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph; he forgot him. <sup>ⓒ</sup>

AMP.2: Pharaoh ( Sesostris II) was extremely angry with his two officials, the chief of the cupbearers and the chief of the bakers.
AMP.3: He put them in confinement in the house of the captain of the guard, in the same prison where Joseph was confined.
AMP.4: The captain of the guard put Joseph in charge of them, and he served them; and they continued to be in custody for some time.
AMP.5: Then the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were confined in the prison, both dreamed a dream in the same night, each man with his [own significant] dream and each dream with its [personal] interpretation.
AMP.6: When Joseph came to them in the morning and looked at them, [he saw that] they were sad and depressed.
AMP.7: So he asked Pharaoh's officials who were in confinement with him in his master's house, "Why do you look so down-hearted today?"
AMP.8: And they said to him, "We have [each] dreamed [distinct] dreams and there is no one to interpret them." So Joseph said to them, "Do not interpretations belong to God? Please tell me [your dreams]."
AMP.9: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, "In my dream there was a grapevine in front of me;
AMP.10: and on the vine were three branches. Then as soon as it budded, its blossoms burst open, and its clusters produced ripe grapes [in rapid succession].
AMP.11: Now Pharaoh's cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup; then I placed the cup into Pharaoh's hand."
AMP.12: Then Joseph said to him, "This is the interpretation of it: the three branches represent three days;
AMP.13: within three more days Pharaoh will lift up your head (present you in public) and restore you to your position; and you will [again] put Pharaoh's cup into his hand just as [you did] when you were his cupbearer.
AMP.14: Only think of me when it goes well with you, and please show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh and get me out of this house.
AMP.15: For in fact I was taken (stolen) from the land of the Hebrews by [unlawful] force, and even here I have done nothing for which they should put me in the dungeon."
AMP.16: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation [of the dream] was good, he said to Joseph, "I also dreamed, and [in my dream] there were three cake baskets on my head;
AMP.17: and in the top basket there were some of all sorts of baked food for Pharaoh, but the birds [of prey] were eating [these foods] out of the basket on my head."
AMP.18: Joseph answered, "This is the interpretation of it: the three baskets represent three days;
AMP.19: within three more days Pharaoh will lift up your head and will hang you on a tree (gallows, pole), and [you will not so much as be given a burial, but] the birds will eat your flesh."
AMP.20: Now on the third day, [which was] the Pharaoh's birthday, he [released the two men from prison and] made a feast for all his servants; and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker [that is, presented them in public] among his servants.
AMP.21: He restored the chief cupbearer to his office, and the cupbearer [once again] put the cup into Pharaoh's hand;
AMP.22: but Pharaoh hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had interpreted [the meaning of the dreams] to them.
AMP.23: Yet [even after all that] the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot [all about] him.

MSG.1: As time went on, it happened that the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt crossed their master, the king of Egypt.
MSG.2: Pharaoh was furious with his two officials, the head cupbearer and the head baker,
MSG.3: and put them in custody under the captain of the guard; it was the same jail where Joseph was held.
MSG.4:
The captain of the guard assigned Joseph to see to their needs.
After they had been in custody for a while,
MSG.5: the king's cupbearer and baker, while being held in the jail, both had a dream on the same night, each dream having its own meaning.
MSG.6: When Joseph arrived in the morning, he noticed that they were feeling low.
MSG.7: So he asked them, the two officials of Pharaoh who had been thrown into jail with him, "What's wrong? Why the long faces?"
MSG.8:
They said, "We dreamed dreams and there's no one to interpret them."
Joseph said, "Don't interpretations come from God? Tell me the dreams."
MSG.9: First the head cupbearer told his dream to Joseph: "In my dream there was a vine in front of me
MSG.10: with three branches on it: It budded, blossomed, and the clusters ripened into grapes.
MSG.11: I was holding Pharaoh's cup; I took the grapes, squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup, and gave the cup to Pharaoh."
MSG.12: Joseph said, "Here's the meaning. The three branches are three days.
MSG.13: Within three days, Pharaoh will get you out of here and put you back to your old work—you'll be giving Pharaoh his cup just as you used to do when you were his cupbearer.
MSG.14: Only remember me when things are going well with you again—tell Pharaoh about me and get me out of this place.
MSG.15: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews. And since I've been here, I've done nothing to deserve being put in this hole."
MSG.16: When the head baker saw how well Joseph's interpretation turned out, he spoke up: "My dream went like this: I saw three wicker baskets on my head;
MSG.17: the top basket had assorted pastries from the bakery and birds were picking at them from the basket on my head."
MSG.18: Joseph said, "This is the interpretation: The three baskets are three days;
MSG.19: within three days Pharaoh will take off your head, impale you on a post, and the birds will pick your bones clean."
MSG.20: And sure enough, on the third day it was Pharaoh's birthday and he threw a feast for all his servants. He set the head cupbearer and the head baker in places of honor in the presence of all the guests.
MSG.21: Then he restored the head cupbearer to his cupbearing post; he handed Pharaoh his cup just as before.
MSG.22: And then he impaled the head baker on a post, following Joseph's interpretations exactly.

NIV.1:
The Cupbearer and the Baker

NIV.2: Pharaoh was angry with his two officials, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker,
NIV.3: and put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, in the same prison where Joseph was confined.
NIV.4:
The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he attended them.
After they had been in custody for some time,
NIV.5: each of the two men—the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were being held in prison—had a dream the same night, and each dream had a meaning of its own.
NIV.6: When Joseph came to them the next morning, he saw that they were dejected.
NIV.7: So he asked Pharaoh’s officials who were in custody with him in his master’s house, “Why are your faces so sad today?”
NIV.8:
“We both had dreams,” they answered, “but there is no one to interpret them.”
Then Joseph said to them, “Do not interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.”
NIV.9: So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream. He said to him, “In my dream I saw a vine in front of me,
NIV.10: and on the vine were three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters ripened into grapes.
NIV.11: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes, squeezed them into Pharaoh’s cup and put the cup in his hand.”
NIV.12: “This is what it means,” Joseph said to him. “The three branches are three days.

NIV.15: For I was forcibly carried off from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing to deserve being put in a dungeon.”
NIV.16: When the chief baker saw that Joseph had given a favorable interpretation, he said to Joseph, “I too had a dream: On my head were three baskets of bread.
NIV.17: In the top basket were all kinds of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.”
NIV.18: “This is what it means,” Joseph said. “The three baskets are three days.

NIV.22: but he hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had said to them in his interpretation.

NET.1: After these things happened, the cupbearer to the king of Egypt and the royal baker offended their master, the king of Egypt.
